cells.tense: The order you are keeping here is holding, and it is yours.
cells.act: wait until you know which part matters, then begin with that part
cells.ask: For a while, when you sit down to tend this, hold off arranging anything until one part asks for you. Start there, and leave the rest unsorted.
cells.core:
You are holding a shape for something still developing, and the shape is doing its job. Few rules, and they hold. What you set three weeks ago is still serving this week, so the thing can grow inside it instead of around it.

The work left is not more structure. It is knowing which part wants you today. Before you arrange anything, wait a beat and notice the one piece that has been asking — the form that is not moving, the small thing you keep stepping around. Start there. What that leaves undone is not failure. It is the cost of doing the right part first, and it comes back around.
cells.sheetLine: The shape you keep is working. Start where it asks.
cells.place: where something is still growing and mostly needs conditions, not orders

cells.tense: You are building the frame for a thing that has not yet decided what it is.
cells.act: step back far enough to see the whole arrangement
cells.ask: Before the next change you make to how this is set up, take in the whole arrangement at once and say what it is for, not what goes in it.
cells.core:
Something under your care keeps getting built before it has decided what it is. There are rules for a stage that has not arrived, and a shape you keep tightening where nothing has grown into it yet. The scaffolding does more than the thing inside it. What wanted room is getting a container.

Take in the whole arrangement in one look — not this corner, the whole shape — and say what it is for. Not what you put in it, what it is for. One look from that distance usually shows which parts carry weight and which are holding the thing shut. Then keep what carries and drop what only guards.
cells.sheetLine: You're framing a thing before it knows its shape.

cells.tense: The pieces of this have been waiting for an order that did not come together.
cells.act: break the habit that was propping it
cells.ask: Take one routine you keep up with this only out of habit and set it down. Watch what happens over the weeks without it.
cells.core:
Something you are tending has pieces that have not assembled. Lists get made and dropped. The same three tasks circle, and what is actually growing keeps getting buried under the version that is not. The trouble is not effort. One arrangement keeps getting propped because it used to work, and the propping takes the attention the living part needs.

Take one routine you keep up out of habit — a schedule, a way you have sorted this — and set it down. Watch what happens over the weeks. If it was holding the real thing, the time will feel it. If you were the only thing holding it, the ground under it goes clear, and you can see what is actually here.

cells.tense: The shape this growing thing has been holding is yours, and you have been calling it nothing.
cells.act: mark the end of it with a plain act
cells.ask: Catch yourself setting something here in order, and leave one plain mark that it came from you — a date in the margin, a change you keep.
cells.core:
A shape you keep goes unowned while people lean on it. The thing runs, people find what they need, and you move on feeling like nothing here is held — because it goes unmarked. The organizing is not hidden. It is just unsigned, so it does not count to you, and the part of you that would grow from knowing it is busy holding what nobody has credited.

Catch the moment you set something in order without noticing — the plan, the arrangement made before anyone asked — and leave one plain mark that it came from you. A date in the margin, a small change you keep. Not a claim. Just the loop between what you do and what you know you do.
cells.sheetLine: You keep a shape nobody marks, including you.
